name: Fujitsu Tofu Interconnect 2
description: Fujitsu’s second-generation Tofu interconnect retained the six-dimensional mesh/torus design and integrated the controller into the FX100 node processor. It was used in the National Institute for Fusion Science’s updated Plasma Simulator.

date.basis: The Hot Interconnects presentation deck gives the day.

events.statement: Fujitsu's team presented the Tofu2 interconnect design, integrating the network controller into the processor chip while retaining the six-dimensional mesh/torus.

evidence.supports: Dated slides contrast Tofu1 and Tofu2 and describe chip integration and network topology.

date.basis: The NIFS announcement dates the updated system's start of operation to 1 June.

events.statement: Tofu2 entered operation in the Fujitsu PRIMEHPC FX100 installed for the updated Plasma Simulator at NIFS in Toki, Gifu.

evidence.supports: The institute identifies the system and dates operation at its location.
The independent benchmark list identifies the NIFS installation's Tofu2 interconnect.
The designers identify Tofu2 as the FX100 interconnect.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated designer presentation establishes the public design account. The NIFS installation dates a subsequent deployed instance.

research.note: Fujitsu identifies the development sequence. The graph relation remains a candidate pending independent informative corroboration of the precise inheritance.

places.note: Witnessed deployment at NIFS in Toki, Gifu.

links.statement: Which parts of the original Tofu design deployed in K carried through to Tofu2?
links.scope: Interconnect design across K and the FX100-era Tofu2, including original Tofu on the FX10.
links.finding: Fujitsu describes continuity of the six-dimensional topology and the shift to processor-chip integration. The precise inheritance awaits independent informative corroboration.

evidence.supports: Fujitsu credits K’s original Tofu and identifies network topology as retained and integration as the generational change.
The report names K and FX100 as the earlier deployed Tofu generations. Its technical comparison closely follows the Fujitsu account.
